turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I came in because my mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. Like, I'll be at work, looking at the road-closure forms or holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps I’ve done for years. It’s a really heavy paddle, actually. A lot of drivers go past and probably think it’s just cheap plastic, but the one the county gave me has this metal pole that gets absolutely freezing in the mornings. 

I tried wearing those wool gloves my sister knit for me to help with the cold. She used this imported alpaca yarn she bought on her trip to Peru. She talks about that trip all the time, how she hiked up Machu Picchu and it rained the entire way up, so her boots were ruined. I told her the gloves were beautiful, but honestly, the yarn makes my wrists break out in this awful red rash. I had to buy a special cream at Walgreens just to get it to stop itching. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just... I stare at the road and completely forget what I'm supposed to be doing.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the road paddle to the cold, to their sister's gloves, a trip to Peru, and a rash, before losing track of the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient reports their mind going blank and being unable to remember steps for tasks they have done for years.

turns.doctor_question: When your mind goes blank, do you ever feel like someone else is controlling your thoughts or that there are hidden messages in the things you see around you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah... I mean, I don't know about controlling my thoughts, but there are definitely messages. Like, I am completely convinced that the city trucks and the police radios have been keeping tabs on me. They drive by my work site all the time. The sanitation trucks are the worst, they're supposed to be on a completely different route on Tuesdays. 

My uncle actually used to drive a truck, a big eighteen-wheeler hauling lumber down from Oregon. Oregon is supposed to be gorgeous, I’ve always wanted to see the coast there, but I hear the rain is just relentless. Kind of like Seattle, I guess, where it just drizzles for nine months straight. I couldn't deal with that kind of dampness, it gets into your bones. 

But anyway, they use those radios to track where I am. And the road signs... when the digital construction signs flash, I know it is a message specifically about me. My sister tells me it’s not, she says I'm just reading into the normal traffic alerts, but she just doesn't see what's right in front of her. It happens at church, too. When someone lowers their voice, I know it's a message about me. Which is rude, honestly, especially at a church function. We had a potluck last Sunday and Mrs. Higgins brought this macaroni salad that was just swimming in mayonnaise. I really don't understand why people drown pasta in mayo, it completely ruins the texture. You really have to use a light vinaigrette with some celery if you want it to taste fresh. 

But yeah, when they whisper over the buffet table, I know exactly what they're doing. Wait, did you ask about the police radios?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses fixed beliefs that city trucks and police radios are tracking them, and that flashing signs and people whispering are hidden messages specifically about them.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, wandering off-topic to discuss their uncle, Oregon weather, and macaroni salad recipes before returning to the original point.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any periods where you felt so depressed or so high/energetic that it significantly changed how you functioned for several days or weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response:
High or energetic? No, definitely not high. But depressed... yeah. It's been really bad. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest, like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. 

And my bedroom floors are that cheap laminate wood, you know? They get incredibly cold in the winter. I actually had to buy these thick memory foam slippers from Target just to be able to walk to the kitchen to make coffee. Target has completely rearranged their store layout, by the way. Have you been lately? It makes absolutely no sense. I went in there last month just to get some Tide pods and somehow ended up in the patio and gardening aisle. I don't even have a garden, I'm in a second-floor apartment. I tried growing a little sweet basil in a window box last spring, but it got absolutely covered in aphids. Those little green bugs just drain the life out of the plants. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, told me to spray them with dish soap and water, but I think I used way too much soap because the leaves just turned brown and crispy. Dawn dish soap is great for grease, though. I use it on my work boots when they get road tar on them from the paving crews. Tar is just impossible to get off once it sets into the leather. 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, just that heavy, ruined feeling every single morning.

turns.doctor_question: During the times when you feel that heavy, hollow sadness, do you notice that the thoughts about the police radios and the signs being messages for you become significantly more intense or frequent?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah... yeah, they definitely happen at the same time. For months now, it's just been this awful stretch where I wake up with that sadness, and I just feel so guilty about everything, and I barely eat. And I just... I wish I wouldn't wake up at all. And that's exactly when the voices and the messages from the trucks and the radios are happening, too. 

It's hard to even eat when I feel like that. I used to love making breakfast, like those fluffy scrambled eggs with a little bit of cheese folded in. You have to take them off the heat right before they look done, otherwise they get rubbery. My sister always burns her eggs. She leaves the pan on high heat and just walks away to check her phone. She's always on her phone, scrolling through those videos of people renovating old camper vans. I don't get the appeal of living in a van, honestly. Where do you even put all your stuff? I have way too many winter coats to fit in a van. I bought this really heavy down parka last year because standing out on the road in February is brutal. The wind just cuts right through you. 

But yeah, the sadness and the messages... they've been happening together for months. Wait, did you ask about the trucks again?

turns.doctor_question: Have there been any periods of at least two weeks where you felt the messages from the trucks and radios were happening, but you did not feel that heavy, hollow sadness?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually... before the depression got so deep, there was a stretch, maybe a few weeks or so? I was still getting up, going to work at the crosswalk, still making it to church on Sundays. But I was already hearing my name in the static, you know? And the signs were already flashing those messages about me. 

Speaking of the signs, they just put up a new digital one over on 4th Street. It's one of those solar-powered ones, which I guess is good for the environment, but the glare off the solar panel is blinding if you're standing at the right angle. My supervisor, Tom, he's supposed to make sure our posts are safe, but he's always in his truck with the AC blasting. He drives this massive Ford F-250, lifted, tires the size of a small car. I don't know how he affords the gas, honestly. Gas prices are just ridiculous right now. I was at the pump the other day and it was almost four dollars a gallon. I remember when I was in college, getting my degree, I could fill up my little Honda Civic for like twenty bucks. That car was so reliable. It was this awful pale green color, kind of like split pea soup, but it ran forever. I had to sell it when the transmission finally went out, which was a nightmare because the mechanic tried to charge me double what the part was worth. You really have to watch out for mechanics, they see a woman come in and they just assume you don't know anything about cars. 

But anyway, yeah, I was still functioning okay, not feeling that heavy sadness yet, but the messages and the radios were definitely already happening. Wait, did you ask if I was still going to work?

turns.patient_response:
Well, altogether? The voices and the feeling that the signs and the trucks and the radios are sending me those messages... it's been about a year and four months now. 

It started right around the time they repaved the intersection at 5th and Main. You know, when they do that, the smell of the hot asphalt is just overwhelming. It sticks to your clothes. I had this one reflective vest, the bright yellow kind, and I swear it permanently smelled like tar after that week. I had to throw it out and get a new one from the supply closet, but the new ones are so stiff. They don't bend with you when you move your arms to hold the stop sign up. My shoulder actually started hurting because the vest was pulling on my neck. I tried soaking it in fabric softener, the lavender kind. I love lavender. I have a little lavender plant on my windowsill at home, but it's not doing so well right now. I think I might be overwatering it. You're only supposed to water them when the soil is completely dry, but it just looks so sad and droopy, I always want to give it a little drink. 

But yeah, a year and four months of the messages and the static. It's been a long time. Wait, did you ask about the asphalt?
